articleTitle: Impact of Vortex Generators on Archimedes Spiral Wind Turbine
abstract: This paper presents a novel method for studying the effect of vortex generators on an Archimedes Spiral Wind Turbine (ASWT), demonstrating improvements in power output and efficiency compared to conventional designs. The Archimedes spiral wind turbine design features three blades characterized by a uniform spiral growth. Vortex generators are small devices that enhance flow attachment by creating vortices. This study explores the potential benefits of integrating vortex generators with ASWTs to enhance Horizontal Axis Wind Turbine (HAWT) systems and applications. Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) simulations were conducted to assess and compare the effects of these generators on the ASWT. SolidWorks is used for model creation whereas Ansys Fluent for simulations. The analysis consisted of two domains: a rotating domain and a stationary domain. The CFD analysis was performed using the Reynolds-Averaged Navier-Stokes (RANS) equations. At a wind speed of 8 m/s, the results indicated that the inclusion of vortex generators increased power output by 7.2%, 7.9%, 5.2%, 7.9%, and 24.1% at Tip Speed Ratios (TSR) of 1.0, 1.32, 2.0, 2.5, and 3 respectively. Consequently, power output is enhanced at higher TSRs, concluding that vortex generators improved the performance of the ASWT.

articleTitle: Low Inertia Challenges and Mitigation Strategies
abstract: The integration of renewable energy sources (RES) is significantly changing the power generation landscape. This shift results in low-inertia grids that are more vulnerable to stability issues and rapid frequency fluctuations. This paper addresses the challenges associated with the low inertia grid and explores various inertia emulating strategies.

articleTitle: Optimizing Solar Power Forecasting by Employing Various Machine Learning and Deep Learning Strategies for Enhanced Accuracy and Reliability
abstract: Before investing in a solar power system, it is critical to properly assess the viability of solar power generation. This evaluation is carried out using a detailed forecasting procedure that entails examining a variety of parameters to predict the probable success and efficiency of using solar energy in that specific geographical location. In the pursuit of advancing solar power forecasting, this research explores a range of machine learning and deep learning strategies to optimize accuracy and reliability. Through a comprehensive evaluation, the Random Forest Regression (RFR) model emerges as the most effective, exhibiting lower Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) and higher R-squared (R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>) values compared to alternative models. These results underscore the significance of leveraging diverse and sophisticated methodologies for achieving superior solar power predictions. The study contributes valuable insights to the field, emphasizing the importance of model selection in enhancing the performance of solar energy forecasting systems.

articleTitle: Deep Learning for Underwater Condition Monitoring of Offshore Energy Installations
abstract: Underwater structural health monitoring (SHM) is essential for protecting offshore structures from continuous challenges such as biofouling, corrosion, spalling, and cracks caused by harsh underwater conditions. Traditional inspection methods are time-consuming, expensive, and prone to human error. In this study, we propose an autonomous underwater robotic system integrated with deep learning algorithms to overcome these limitations. The system utilizes autonomous underwater robots equipped with optical cameras to collect high-resolution visual data. Collected images are preprocessed using denoising techniques to address visibility challenges, and defects are detected and classified using a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) trained on annotated underwater defect datasets. Preliminary results indicate that the system significantly improves defect detection accuracy, achieving an 87% increase over conventional approaches. Additionally, the automated system reduces inspection costs by 93% and enhances operational efficiency by minimizing downtime and improving data reliability. By integrating robotics and deep learning(DL), this study enables proactive maintenance strategies, ensuring the long-term sustainability, performance, and resilience of critical underwater infrastructure.

articleTitle: Modelling and Electrothermal Simulation of Temperature Rise in a SF6-Free MV Circuit-Breaker
abstract: Active research for replacement of SF6 is more complex and requires the validation of many criteria to ensure proper operation of the circuit-breaker under normal conditions. Among these criteria, there is the temperature rise of the conductors which must not exceed a limit in accordance with the IEC or IEEE standard. After completion of dielectric type tests, it was proved that pure nitrogen at 2.5 bar can replace SF6 at 1.5 bar in a VOX 38kV outdoor circuit breaker by meeting the dielectric requirements. This article deals with the simulation of the temperature rise in different elements of the circuit breaker with these two gases: SF6 and N2. The coupling of computational fluid dynamics and computational electro magnetics and non-isothermal flow are used to determine the temperature rise of the breaker. Simulation tests were performed at rated nominal current 2000 A, 50 Hz with specifications of IEEE and IEC standards and finally, the requirements were met with SF6 at 1.5 bar whose results are in good agreement with those of the experimental tests carried out and allowing to predict the results with N2 at 2.5 bar with numerical model build. The results with N2 show a better thermal behavior of all the conductors of the breaker than with SF6 and conclude that pure nitrogen at 2.5 bar can replace SF6 at 1.5 bar in a 38kV outdoor circuit-breaker.

articleTitle: Control-oriented Run-time Computer Memory Modeling and Energy Management
abstract: This study investigates control-oriented computer memory system modeling and runtime energy optimization. Two different common memory types, namely, DRAM and PCRAM, were identified and analyzed for their data exchange cycle times, namely, Write, Read, and Idle operations, and associated energy consumption levels. Once the respective transfer functions were obtained, their open-loop responses for illustrative data operations were analyzed. Then, the memory system transfer functions were utilized in a typical feedback control system configuration and different controller were evaluated for corresponding energy consumption characteristics and amounts. Numerical results imply that the feedback control systems offer runtime memory system energy optimization opportunity for large computer systems.

articleTitle: Green AI: Optimizing Energy Efficiency of Workloads for Sustainable Data Centers
abstract: In the rapidly evolving landscape of artificial intelligence, the energy demands of AI workloads, particularly those involving deep learning and large-scale data processing, pose significant challenges for data centers. This paper presents a comprehensive solution for energy-aware scheduling of AI workloads, aimed at optimizing energy usage, reducing operational costs, and minimizing environmental impact. By dynamically managing AI workloads in response to real-time energy availability from power grid, the proposed system ensures optimal resource utilization and performance-per-watt ratios. The system's architecture integrates key components such as AI workload information collection, energy profiling, workload categorization, and dynamic scheduling, enabling efficient management of computational resources. This approach not only enhances the performance and reliability of AI systems but also leads to substantial cost savings and better scalability as AI applications grow in complexity. As AI continues to integrate into diverse sectors, the demand for efficient and sustainable AI operations will only increase. Energy-aware scheduling emerges as a pivotal strategy to meet this demand, ensuring that AI advancements are both economically viable and environmentally responsible. By adopting these innovative scheduling techniques, organizations can achieve a balance between high performance and energy efficiency, driving forward with enhanced efficiency and sustainability in the competitive AI landscape.

articleTitle: Practical Guide for End Users: Up-Tower Wind Generator Onsite Rotor Lead Identification
abstract: The rapid growth of the wind energy sector has made generator availability and reliability increasingly critical. When a wind generator is offline during wind availability, operators face significant revenue losses, and traditional generator removal for testing or repairs is costly and time-consuming. To address this challenge, the wind generator repair industry has developed specialized up-tower testing methods, enabling field service technicians to diagnose issues without removing the generator. This paper presents a step-by-step procedure for identifying rotor leads on double-fed induction generators (DFIGs) and wound rotor induction generators (WRIGs) onsite, using standard test equipment. By eliminating the need for generator removal, this approach significantly reduces downtime, enhances service efficiency, and allows wind farm owners and technicians to perform first-line diagnostics quickly and effectively.

articleTitle: Resilient Operation of DC Standalone Microgrids: Experimental Validation of Hybrid RNN-PI Control for Pulse Load Management
abstract: Effective energy storage system (ESS) management is critical for enhancing the performance of standalone DC microgrids, particularly when integrating renewable energy sources such as photovoltaic (PV) or wind systems. This research describes a new hybrid control technique to improve DC microgrid operations' efficiency and resiliency, especially when handling critical loads. This research presents a hybrid closed-loop control technique that uses Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs) and Proportional-Integral (PI) controllers to address the complex issues of dynamic load situations and transient disturbances. The RNN evaluates voltage errors to generate accurate reference currents, which the PI controllers then adjust to improve the performance of the bidirectional converter. Unlike standard PI-PI controls, our hybrid approach is particularly effective at regulating pulsed power loads (PPLs) and enhancing system response to transitory situations. The experimental results show that the RNN-PI control scheme significantly improves voltage regulation and transient responsiveness, exceeding conventional performance and resilience techniques. This approach provides a convincing solution for enhancing microgrid systems' stability and efficiency in various real-world applications.

articleTitle: Parameter Estimation of Unreported PVs using Distribution System State Estimation Algorithm
abstract: The growing trend of solar photovoltaic systems within electric power distribution networks can potentially introduce challenges such as reverse power flow and overvoltage issues. This makes accurate knowledge of and the ability to validate rooftop photovoltaic system location and power generation valuable to distribution system operators. In modern power distribution systems, accurate information on the location, status, and settings of all controllable assets mitigates operational risk and supports coordination of grid-edge devices. This paper presents a state estimation algorithm for distribution systems that can accurately estimate photovoltaic system injections. Specifically, the algorithm 1) detects unregistered rooftop photovoltaics by estimating the injections of hypothetical systems at behind-the-meter locations, 2) identifies inverter settings for unregistered systems, and 3) detects incorrect inverter settings for registered systems. The algorithm is implemented as a state estimator federate of the Open Energy Data Initiative Systems Integration platform. The proposed method was shown to correctly identify unregistered photovoltaic systems and power factor settings using a combination of coarse forecasts and simulated smart meter and substation measurements in demonstrations with the IEEE 4-bus, IEEE 13-bus, and IEEE 123-bus test systems under various scenarios.

articleTitle: Guidelines for Economic and Installation Environment-Based Selection of Overhead Transmission Conductors
abstract: This paper provides guidelines for transmission grid planners to improve conductor selection in capacity upgrade projects. Proposed guidelines are developed by implementing a formalized methodology that pre-selects feasible conductors based on ampacity and sag constraints, then evaluates the net-present cost (NPC) of each project over the entire lifetime of the line. Results emphasize the impact of conductor selection on projects' cost-benefit value, and recommend for grid planners to: i) consider various parameters for conductor selection (technical, economic, and new power generation), ii) evaluate projects over the entire line lifetime, iii) associate conductor selection with investment option selection, and iv) better estimate the duration of line use to capture the impact of losses and congestion.

articleTitle: CPS-DERMS: Cyber-Physical Security and Impact Analysis of DERMS Against MITM Attacks
abstract: The growing integration of Distributed Energy Resources (DERs) into modern power grids, managed via DER Management Systems (DERMS), has introduced significant cybersecurity challenges. Communication vulnerabilities in DERMS architecture create opportunities for adversarial attacks, such as Man-in-the-Middle (MITM), that intercept and manipulate critical data flows, disrupting grid operations and compromising reliability. This paper investigates MITM attacks targeting three critical nodes in DER-DERMS communication: (i) DER gateway routers, (ii) inter-router pathways, and (iii) DERMS gateway routers. To analyze these vulnerabilities, we developed CPS-DERMS, a multi-co-simulation hardware-in-the-loop testbed integrating grid-side simulations with OPAL-RT, large-scale cyber simulations using NS-3, and an indige-nous Python-based DERMS platform. The study demonstrates innovative strategies for executing MITM attacks, including maintaining payload integrity and bypassing detection mechanisms, while highlighting the critical vulnerabilities within DER-DERMS communication systems. We considered a real utility's DER-integrated distribution grid as a case study. Experimental results reveal that MITM attacks can cause overvoltages, reactive power imbalances, and increased tap-changer operations, significantly degrading power quality and grid reliability.

articleTitle: Real-Time Inertia Estimation and Validation Using PMU Data and the Swing Equation in Power Systems
abstract: This paper presents a method to estimate power system inertia in real-time using Phasor Measurement Unit (PMU) data and the swing equation. Inertia is essential for maintaining power system stability during disturbances. The method calculates both electrical and mechanical power from PMU data and uses this information to estimate inertia by using Matlab. Then it validates the results by comparing calculated values with real measurements of the rate of change of frequency (ROCOF). Further validation is performed using data from a real-world generation trip event. The outcomes show that the proposed method is accurate, with minimal error, making it suitable for real-time applications.

articleTitle: Coordinated Deliverable Energy Flexibility from EV Aggregators in Distribution Networks
abstract: This paper presents a coordinated framework to optimize electric vehicle (EV) charging considering grid constraints and system uncertainties. The proposed framework consists of two optimization models. In particular, the distribution system operator (DSO) solves the first model to optimize the amount of deliverable energy flexibility that can be obtained from EV ag-gregators. To address the uncertainties of loads and solar energy generation, a hybrid robust/stochastic approach is employed, enabling the transformation of uncertainty-related constraints into a set of equivalent deterministic constraints. Once the DSO has computed the optimal energy flexibility, each aggregator utilizes the second optimization model to optimize the charging schedule for its respective fleet of EVs. Numerical simulations are performed on a modified IEEE 33-bus distribution network to illustrate the efficiency of the proposed framework.

articleTitle: Machine Learning-Based Framework for Online State of Health Assessment and End-of-Life Prediction in Commercial Lithium-Ion Batteries
abstract: Lithium-ion batteries (LIBs) are an essential and versatile energy source for portable electronics, grid energy storage, and electric vehicles. To meet the increasing demand for energy, it is crucial to understand physical changes to further improve LIBs performance and safety. State of health (SOH) is a metric that indicates how safe LIBs are for operation. This work presents a comprehensive framework for SOH assessment of LIBs. The proposed framework was validated using data from commercial LIBs tested at 1C/1C (charge/discharge), at different temperatures and different depths of discharge (DOD). Reference performance tests (RPTs) were periodically conducted until lithium-ion cells (LICs) reached the end of life. Differential voltage analysis (DVA) was used to acquire relevant physical parameters from RPTs. The continuous monitoring of DVA provided updates about LIC degradation based on internal resistance, slippages, active masses, and stoichiometries of both electrodes during the cycling process. For prediction of degradation mechanisms and end of life (EOL), a machine learning model based on Random Forest was integrated into a Raspberry Pi computer. This affordable computer enabled remote monitoring of LICs performance, which transmitted SOH and degradation data to a cloud-based service. Results indicate that LICs cycled at 100% DOD experienced greater cathode material loss compared to those cycled at lower DODs. The RF model, running on a Raspberry Pi computer, achieved a processing time of approximately 2.9 seconds and demonstrated an accuracy of 86.67%. This attained accuracy indicates the potential of this affordable framework to be employed in real-time (online) assessments of SOH in either small or larger LIBs with different chemistries.

articleTitle: PEM-Based Green Hydrogen Plant: Harmonic Issues and Mitigation using Active and Passive Filters 1
abstract: Grid compliance for harmonic current injection of hydrogen generation plant based on proton exchange membrane (PEM) electrolyzer technologies is of particular importance for a hydrogen-based economy. This paper studies harmonic mitigation strategy using commercial-off-the-shelf (COTS) active harmonic filter (AHF) product in 6-pulse and 12-pulse thyristor rectifier based green hydrogen plant's electrical designs. It shows that for multi-megawatt (MW) plant a modular design of the AHFs is a good option. A 6-pulse rectifier powered plant needs a passive filter to mitigate the large 5<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sup> order harmonic, while AHFs can be used to mitigate harmonics higher than the 5<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sup> order. A 12-pulse rectifier can use AHFs to mitigate 7th order and up harmonics, while using an 11<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sup> order passive filter to meet the IEEE 519 requirements.

articleTitle: Integrating Machine Learning Models to Enhance the Efficiency of a Desalination Process
abstract: Freshwater scarcity is a critical global challenge, with over two billion people lacking access to safe drinking water. Desalination technologies, particularly Air Gap Membrane Distillation (AGMD) offer a sustainable solution by utilizing superhydrophobic membranes to enhance efficiency and reduce environmental impact. This study integrates material science and machine learning (ML) to optimize AGMD systems, employing Ridge Regression (RR), Support Vector Regression (SVR), and Decision Tree Regression (DTR) models to predict important desalination metrics such as desalination water produced and salt rejection rates. The results demonstrate RR's superior performance with a better R-squared and lowest mean square error (MSE), highlighting its robustness for handling multicollinearity. SVR effectively captures nonlinear relationships, while DTR provides interpretability despite its overfitting tendencies. This research advances sustainable desalination by combining inno-vative materials with ML-driven optimization, paving the way for scalable and environmentally friendly water management solutions.

articleTitle: Electric Vehicle Charging System Controller Analysis and Synthesis
abstract: This research investigates a type of converter and charging system in terms of closed-loop design for a potentially superior charging system for electric vehicle, resulting in better battery life and energy efficiency. A recent rectifier-charging system is analyzed in terms of the controller and given controller types. A baseline with the existing design was implemented and different controller combinations, as part of the proportional-integral-derivative controller, were investigated about their effects on the charging circuit operations and related battery performance levels. Simulation results imply that different controllers result in different output characteristics, and potential controller optimizations, in addition to the circuit operations, are likely to yield superior charging operations.

articleTitle: An Environmental Metric for Vulnerability Assessment of Overhead Power Lines to Extreme Weather Events
abstract: Extreme weather events, driven by climate change, are causing widespread, long-duration power outages with significant societal and infrastructural impacts. This paper presents a two-dimensional metric for quantifying the vulnerability of overhead power lines by integrating meteorological and geographical factors. Vulnerability scores are calculated for each dimension using the L2 norm of the main principal components of the data, then aggregated through Pareto ranking to determine the overall vulnerability of overhead lines. The framework was validated through a case study within the Connexus Energy service area, demonstrating alignment between computed vulnerability scores and historical outage data. This methodology provides utilities with a practical tool for enhancing power grid resilience by identifying the best candidate lines for targeted mitigation strategies.

articleTitle: Performance Optimization and Bandgap Tuning of Ba(Zr(1-x)Tix)S3 Perovskite Solar Cells Via Titanium Alloying for High-Efficiency Photovoltaic Systems
abstract: Recent advancements in photovoltaic technologies have concentrated on lead-free perovskite materials such as BaZrS3, noted for its effective absorption of visible light and environmental stability. Alloying BaZrS3 with titanium (Ti) represents a significant advancement in improving the efficiency of perovskite solar cells. Kesterite materials, including CZTGS, have garnered interest for their effectiveness as both absorbers and hole-transport materials (HTMs), presenting synergistic possibilities in advanced solar cell designs. This study presents a novel solar cell design that integrates Ti alloying into a BaZrS3-based absorber, resulting in the formation of the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{Ba}(\mathbf{Zr}_{(1-\mathrm{x})}\mathbf{Ti}_{\mathbf{x}})\mathbf{S}_{3}$</tex> compound. The alloying process is examined with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{x}$</tex> values from <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{0}$</tex> to 0.04, resulting in a bandgap reduction from 1.78 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$e$</tex>V to 1.51 eV. The optimized device structure, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{FTO}/\mathbf{TiO}_{2}/\mathbf{Ba}(\mathbf{Zr}_{0.96}\mathbf{Ti}_{0.04})\mathbf{S}_{3}/\mathbf{CZTGS}/\mathbf{Pt}$</tex>, is attained at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{x}= 0.04$</tex>, which corresponds to a bandgap of 1.51 eV. An analysis of tunable parameters, such as absorber bandgap, thickness, and doping concentration, is conducted in conjunction with an investigation of temperature-dependent performance. The optimized device exhibits notable performance, attaining an open-circuit voltage <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\mathrm{V}_{\text{oc}})$</tex> of 1.18 V, a short-circuit current density <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\mathbf{J}_{\text{sc}})$</tex> of 27.33 mA/cm2, a power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 28.6%, and a fill factor (FF) of 88.9%. The results highlight the considerable potential of this novel design, facilitating the experimental realization of high-efficiency BaZrS3-based perovskite solar cells (PSC).

articleTitle: Modeling Electric Vehicle Charging Load on Power Grid Considering Travel Behavior
abstract: Electric vehicle (EV) usage increases every year, yet there is no accurate model to predict traveling or charging behavior. Current working models present inaccurate data as well as showing the same daily demand at different locations. These models do not consider the variations of human behavior and differences in geographic areas. However, an agent-based modeling (ABM) system is able to track individuals in a simulation to predict their behavior. NetLogo is an ABM platform implemented to show the behavior of EVs. Through the ABM simulation, travelers were simulated and recorded to predict their future load demand realistically and accurately on the grid. This simulation showed different peak times and load amounts between locations and slight differences in each iteration as expected. These results show a more accurate prediction of future EV load demand based on the input data such as vehicle type ratio, number of vehicles, and average range of city.

articleTitle: Background to the Fore: AI and Software Patent Eligibility
abstract: Software and AI seem destined to both help and harm efforts toward sustainability. In part, AI's role may depend on its patent eligibility. Software faces an uphill battle to qualify for patents. Tension between the Supreme Court's Alice decision (a patent killer) and the increasing prevalence of AI patent applications makes understanding the boundary between patent-eligible and -ineligible subject matter more important than ever. This article reviews the latest guidance from the U.S. Patent Office on the patentability of software, including artificial intelligence. An AI invention can become subject-matter eligible through narrow, “practical” applications that solve problems beyond a desired mathematical result or routine automatization.

articleTitle: Navigating the Regulatory Landscape: Roadmap for Successful Phaseout of SF6
abstract: The electric utility industry has long prioritized environmental compliance and Rate Payers-focused policies. As the United States economy and energy demand have grown over the decades, so has the need for more substations and transmission lines to ensure reliable power. SF6 (Sulphur Hexafluoride), a widely used insulation gas in medium voltage to extra-high voltage equipment, offers superior dielectric strength and fast recovery, making it a go-to choice of insulation gas in modern electrical systems. However, SF6 is a potent greenhouse gas, and increasing environmental concerns have led regulators to push for its reduction and eventual elimination. This paper explores strategies for phasing out SF6 from utility systems using game theory including coalition and evolutionary theories, considering the perspectives of key stakeholders such as Utilities, Regulators, Manufacturers, and Rate Payers. We also evaluate the benefits and challenges of a complete SF6 elimination policy thru coalition formation and evolutionary game theory models.

articleTitle: Toward the Impact of Video Luminance on the Energy Consumption of OLED TVs and Viewer Perception
abstract: Video streaming services have become integral to modern digital experiences, yet they present a challenge in balancing perceptual quality with energy efficiency. The climate crisis has underscored the environmental effects of information and communication technologies (ICT), emphasizing the necessity for eco-friendly solutions to minimize ICT's carbon emissions. With video streaming leading Internet traffic, research in this area is more crucial than ever. This paper presents a study on the impact of luminance changes in video streaming on the perceptual quality experienced by end users and the associated energy consumption. Various levels of luminance reduction are investigated in different video bitrates and video characteristics. We also conducted a subjective test with 28 participants to understand how much the video's luminance can be reduced without degrading the visual quality. The results show the tradeoff between visual quality and energy efficiency in video luminance reduction. We found that the optimized level of luminance reduction depends on the video content. Some specific videos can be reduced by 10% of luminance to save up to 14% of energy consumption while maintaining an acceptable visual quality. Some other videos should be reduced by only 4%.

articleTitle: Green AI Solutions for Automated Insect Monitoring to Improve Stored Product Management Systems
abstract: This study presents an integrated AI framework for automated beetle detection in stored product environments, leveraging EfficientNet Lite for feature extraction and XGBoost for classification. The system addresses the challenge of precise species identification in low-resource settings, enhancing postharvest sustainability. Our approach focuses on five stored product beetles: maize weevil (Sitophilus zeamais), red flour beetle (Tribolium castaneum), sawtoothed grain beetle (Oryzaephilus surinamensis), lesser grain borer (Rhyzopertha dominica), and rusty grain beetle (Cryptolestes ferrugineus). Experimental results demonstrate a training accuracy of 98.9% and a testing accuracy of 98.7<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>. Additionally, a performance comparison with other models demonstrates superior resource efficiency. The hybrid attention map (HAM) enhances interpretability by localizing morphological features like antennae, elytra, and body contour. The proposed system achieved a performance optimization score (POS) of 239.2, indicating suitability for real-time IoT-enabled monitoring solutions. Our results indicate significant potential to reduce grain losses and minimize pesticide usage using this detection system.

articleTitle: Enhanced IoT Security for Healthcare: A Lionized Remora Optimization-Based Image Encryption Algorithm with Chaotic Maps
abstract: Storing and safely transmitting data, however, is a basic obstacle that contemporary healthcare management systems encounter. Consequently, in order to encrypt sensitive data and decrease privacy breaches and cyber-attacks caused by unautho-rised users and hackers, this research suggests a new bit-level image encryption technique based on chaotic maps (BCIEA). Our new Internet of Things (IoT) layered approach incorporates generic and extended components for privacy and security, as well as the ability to identify layer. Furthermore, it was discovered that the BCIEA description lacks rigour, leading to undecipherable algorithm specifics. To bypass the confusion module's dynamic mechanism, the technique first converts the all-zero ciphertext into a diffusion-only procedure, and then selects a cypher image whose sum value is equal to the target cypher image. The results of the experiment indicate that the produced secret keys are adequately unique and random to adequately secure the data kept in contemporary healthcare management systems. Time spent encrypting and decrypting data is reduced, and privacy is enhanced, using the suggested method. The proposed method is more efficient and cheaper than its predecessors, according to this study. It also reduces execution time

articleTitle: Case Study: Photovoltaic Power Forecasting in Cold Regions and Potential Improvements Through Machine Learning
abstract: While solar energy holds great promise in addressing climate change and reducing reliance on fossil fuels, its adoption is hindered by inherent variability due to weather conditions and environmental factors. As a potential solution to address these challenges, we developed a multi-source data integration framework utilizing real power measurements from an installed photovoltaic (PV) system, simulation outputs, and a machine learning (ML) model configured to predict and correct the error between simulated and measured power outputs. The ML algorithm leverages a stacking ensemble method to effectively account for complex environmental interactions, such as snow accumulation, temperature, and wind effects leading to significant improvements in forecasting reliability under diverse conditions. By uncovering complex relationships between environmental factors, our approach allows for adjustments during days and months with snowfall, addressing scenarios where traditional forecasters may overlook local phenomena such as snow coverage. Through this project, we utilized ML to predict the discrepancy (error) between simulated and actual power generated by the PV system. Using the developed model in conjunction with a power forecaster provided data that demonstrated the model's ability to minimize prediction errors compared to real power for the PV system installed at South Dakota Mines.

articleTitle: Assessing ChatGPT's Capabilities in Solving Optimization Problems
abstract: ChatGPT is an LLM that has recently emerged as a remarkable artificial intelligence language model. In this paper, we explore ChatGPT v3.5 and ChatGPT v4.0 capabilities and limitations in modeling and solving various types of network optimization problems, emphasizing energy efficiency. Particularly, we test solutions generated by ChatGPT v3.5 and ChatGPT v4 which is integrated with the Wolfram plugin, against solutions generated by the general-algebraic modeling system (GAMS). The results show that Chat-GPT v3.5 and v4 are capable of generating mathematical models for optimization problems while considering power-related metrics, such as energy consumption and cost. Moreover, ChatGPT can be used to generate mathematical models for large optimization problems and solve them.

articleTitle: Towards Robust Building Damage Detection: Leveraging Augmentation and Domain Adaptation
abstract: The increasing frequency of natural disasters neces-sitates efficient building damage detection for effective disaster response. This study addresses limitations in deep learning models, particularly their inability to classify minor as well as major damage classes due to inadequate detection of structural features like edges and corners in satellite images. To overcome these challenges, we propose the utilization of a fusion-based data augmentation technique that combines edge detection, contrast enhancement, and unsharp masking to enhance structural feature detection. We further evaluate the generalizability of this approach using domain adaptation techniques, including supervised fine-tuning and unsupervised Deep CORAL to address domain shifts between source (xBD) and target (Ida-BD) datasets. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed augmentation improves damage classification accuracy by 5–7% in minor and major damage classes and enhances localization accuracy by 2.5%. Additionally, the integration of domain adaptation techniques validates the robustness in handling out-of-domain datasets. By improving structural feature detection and mitigating domain discrepancies, the proposed methodology enhances performance and adaptability of deep learning models for disaster response. This study demonstrates the potential of fusion-based augmentation and domain adaptation to enable reliable and efficient building damage detection in diverse disaster scenarios.

articleTitle: An Efficient Graph-Based Approach for Identifying Attack Patterns in IoT and IIoT Networks
abstract: The growing attack surface and interconnection of the Internet of Things (IoT) and Industrial IoT (IIoT) have presented major cybersecurity issues. This work presents a graph-based analytical approach for IoT and IIoT environment network vulnerabilities assessment and attack pattern recognition. Synthetic graphs were created with the Edge-IIoTset dataset to simulate network traffic in both normal and attack conditions, encompassing Distributed Denial of Service (DDoS) and backdoor assaults. The framework utilizes centrality measurements and temporal traffic analysis to identify crucial nodes, access points, and compro-mised devices. This method offers practical insights for intrusion detection and threat mitigation, emphasizing the capability of graph-based techniques to improve 1oT/IIoT network security. The findings illustrate the scalability and feasibility of the framework for real-time security applications in industrial environments.

articleTitle: Strategic Switch Placement and Renewable Wind Integration Through Network Reconfiguration with the Modified Cheetah Optimizer
abstract: This paper addresses the optimization challenge of strategically placing sectionalizing switches in distribution networks, crucial for reliable electricity supply, especially with the growing integration of renewable sources like wind power. The objective is to minimize total costs, including installation costs, unserved demand, and interruption costs during islanded mode. Using the Modified Cheetah Optimizer and formulating two key objective functions, the paper presents a comprehensive optimization approach that balances cost-effectiveness, reliability, and renewable energy utilization. Case studies demonstrate the approach's effectiveness in minimizing costs, improving reliability, and introducing network reconfiguration as a crucial element for holistic enhancement. These findings offer insightful perspectives on tradeoffs and synergies between cost minimization and reliability enhancement in distribution systems with renewable energy. By adopting a holistic optimization approach, including network reconfiguration, this paper significantly contributes to the development of robust distribution systems in the era of renewable energy integration.

articleTitle: A Convolution Neural Network for Voltage Event Classification at a Photovoltaic Inverter
abstract: This paper presents a convolutional neural network (CNN) developed to identify voltage events in photovoltaic (PV) inverters. The CNN is trained on synthetic data generated using the IEEE 13-bus distribution feeder model and evaluated on field-measured data collected from Energy Northwest's Horn Rapids Solar, Storage, and Training (HRSST) facility. The study focuses on two common voltage events: faults and voltage sags. The CNN is configured to analyze voltage and current waveforms from three-phase PV systems, demonstrating excellent accuracy during training. Field data from the HRSST facility is employed to assess its real-world performance, where the CNN achieves perfect identification of faults and voltage sags in a sample of nine events. This work highlights the potential of the proposed method to enhance PV protection schemes, providing a robust foundation for improved voltage event detection and grid reliability.

articleTitle: The Electromagnetic Field of a High-Power, Air-Core DD Coupler for DWPT
abstract: Dynamic wireless power transfer (DWPT) requires a track in lieu of the single primary or ground assembly (GA) used in static wireless power transfer. The track is embedded in the roadway and is subject to repetitive stress from vehicles traveling over it, thermal cycling, moisture, and chemical exposure, especially de-icing agents. Therefore, some DWPT tracks employ couplers without ferrite cores despite the performance improvement ferrite provides. The DD coupler is widely used as a GA coupler for such DWPT systems. The original design of the DD coupler employed a flat ferrite core backed by a conducting plate to implement a so-called single-sided coupler. Here, we analyze the effect of eliminating the magnetic core and the backing conductive plate from the DD coupler. It is shown that the equivalent multiple representation of the DD coupler changes markedly with the removal of the ferrite core and further with the removal of the conducting plate. It is shown that not only is the magnetic coupling is diminished, but additionally the nature of the extraneous electromagnetic field is fundamentally altered. A new approach is given for recovering the ferrite-driven performance, based on replacing the Amperian currents representing the ferrite with a third winding.

articleTitle: Quantum-Assisted Joint Generation-Transmission Expansion Planning for Modern Power Systems
abstract: Joint generation-transmission expansion planning (JGTEP) expands the set of feasible solutions compared with traditional approaches, but also introduces the challenge of variables proliferation across generations and transmission networks. Quantum computing offers efficiency advantages over classical methods in handling binary variables, presenting a potential to speed up the planning processes. This paper proposes a method to accelerate JGTEP based on a hybrid quantum-classical framework. Firstly, the JGTEP problem is divided into a master problem and a subdual problem by Benders decomposition. Secondly, a classical computer is then employed to generate multiple feasible solutions for the master problem. An initial solution for warm-starting is created together with the reduction of variable dimension under the characteristics of various feasible solutions. On this basis, the master problem is subsequently transformed into a quadratic unconstrained binary optimization problem, efficiently solved by a warm-starting quantum annealing algorithm. Finally, the master problem and subproblem are solved alternately until the complete results are presented.

articleTitle: Using Co-Simulation to Capture Sector Coupling Dynamics in Low-Temperature Anergy Systems
abstract: Anergy networks offer efficient and sustainable district heating and cooling through low operating temperatures. They facilitate flexible decentralized topologies. Because of their inherent need for heat pumps, they create strong dynamic links with electricity infrastructure. Simulating sector-coupled anergy systems is therefore challenging. This paper advocates for co-simulation as a critical enabler for holistically analyzing anergy networks. With co-simulation, independent subsystem simulators are jointly executed. Using a design science-based approach, we create a proof-of-concept simulation setup that incorporates the unique properties of anergy systems. It includes thermal and electrical networks, strong sector coupling via heat pumps and renewable-based power-to-heat, and decentralized producers in a flexible topology. The results highlight the ability of co-simulation to capture complex cross-domain interactions between the thermal and electrical domain. The approach allows for easy scaling of simulation scenarios and seamless integration of new simulation tools. However, validating composite co-simulation models on the system-of-systems level remains challenging. Co-simulation is a crucial tool for exploiting the potential of anergy systems, without sacrificing the dependability of power grids, paving the way for reliable, sector-coupled energy systems.

articleTitle: Sustainable Offshore Power: Integrating BESS for a Greener Future
abstract: The transition to renewable energy globally is accelerating, with Offshore Renewable Energy (ORE) sources such as wind, wave, and tidal energy becoming key players in reducing CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> emissions. However, due to the intermittent nature of these resources, maintaining grid stability and ensuring a consistent power supply poses serious challenges. Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS) have emerged as a viable solution to these challenges, offering improved grid reliability, energy efficiency, and sustainability. This paper seeks to study the integration of BESS into ORE systems and its ability to create a more sustainable and flexible power grid. It will examine the types of BESS technologies available, their applications in ORE environments, and their benefits regarding grid stability, energy efficiency, and environmental impact. Moreover, the brief overview of utilizing BESS is highlighted for policymakers focusing on key challenges and policy recommendations.

articleTitle: Analysis of Ocean Wave Energy-Driven Desalination Methods for Sustainable Water Production
abstract: This paper investigates the potential of wave energy to drive a desalination system (DS) for sustainable water production, addressing the increasing need for innovative solutions to global water scarcity. Initially, simulation studies are carried out utilizing the National Renewable Energy Laboratory's oscillating surge wave energy converter (OSWEC) model to generate the high-pressure flow required for reverse osmosis (RO) desalination to explore the effects of varying the number of parallel membranes, piston areas, and ocean states on permeate flow and water salinity. This fundamental work provides critical insights into optimizing DS performance and was used to create an ocean wave energy-driven electrical desalination plant that uses a floating buoy and spar paired with a slider crank mechanism to convert wave energy into electrical power. The system is equipped with a maximum power point tracking (MPPT) control algorithm, which drives a rotary positive displacement pump to enhance RO efficiency. Six ocean states are chosen to mimic various deployment situations along the USA West Coast, resulting in a maximum permeate flow rate (PFR) ranging from 155 to 225 gallons per minute. This study advances renewable energy applications for desalination, offering eco-friendly solutions to water scarcity while aligning with global sustainable development goals.

Index Terms: West Coast Of The United States

articleTitle: Dynamic Modeling and Fault Response Analysis of SMR-Integrated Power Grid
abstract: Small Modular Reactors (SMRs) are an emerging technology with load-following capabilities, offering significant potential for enhancing grid stability and resilience. This paper presents the development of an SMR model by replacing an existing generator in the IEEE 39-bus system with a synchronous machine round rotor configured to reflect the operational characteristics of an SMR. The paper focuses on analyzing the dynamic fault response of the SMR at various operating levels, including minimum generation, half, and maximum capacity. Key metrics such as terminal voltage (p.u.) are evaluated to assess the SMR's ability to maintain stability during and after fault scenarios. By examining the SMR's performance under different generation conditions, this paper provides valuable insights into the feasibility of integrating SMRs into modern power systems and their contributions to grid stability during transient events.

articleTitle: Protecting Inverter-Based Resources: Transformer Configuration Impacts and Incremental Focused Directional Protection Enhancements
abstract: Inverter-based resources (IBRs) exhibit distinct short-circuit characteristics that challenge traditional protective relays designed for systems dominated by synchronous generators. While research often focuses on IBRs' positive-sequence currents during faults, their zero- and negative-sequence responses under unsymmetrical faults remain underexplored. Factors such as transformer configurations and grounding methods further complicate the design of protection schemes relying on these sequence components. This paper enhances the understanding of IBR short-circuit behavior during both symmetrical and unsymmetrical faults and investigates the impact of various transformer configurations on these behaviors. We highlight the limitations of traditional protective relays in safeguarding IBRs due to their constrained fault current levels, minimal negative-sequence components, and, in many cases, the absence of zero-sequence currents. To address these challenges, a novel incremental focused directional protection scheme is introduced. This approach offers enhanced fault detection capabilities under the complex conditions posed by high renewable energy penetration and diverse transformer configurations. The proposed method provides a robust solution for ensuring reliable protection in modern power systems with high integration of IBRs, contributing to improved grid stability and resilience.

articleTitle: High Voltage DC Transmission Within Interconnected Systems: Review of Standards and Models for Planning Studies
abstract: The advancements in converter technology and the economic and renewable energy benefits are making High Voltage DC transmission a desirable transmission expansion solution even within a synchronous interconnected system. This would lead to co-existence of DC and AC lines in parallel within an interconnected system. This calls for new standards and codes for operation and appropriate models to support system planning studies. This short review papers focuses on the recent developments in this regard and presents potential avenues for innovation to support High Voltage DC transmission.

articleTitle: Enhancing Reliability and Efficiency: Design Innovations for 2.3 MW Wind Generators
abstract: This paper evaluates the challenges and solutions associated with the 2.3 MW wind generator class, a widely deployed platform that remains critical to renewable energy infrastructure. As the installed base of wind generators continues to expand, ensuring long-term reliability and efficiency becomes a key priority for operators. This study identifies common failure modes and investigates engineering design improvements aimed at enhancing reliability, reducing repair complexity, and lowering overall lifecycle costs. A primary challenge in assessing wind generator performance is the lack of detailed efficiency and loss breakdowns from OEMs, making direct validation difficult. To address this, the paper introduces a novel analytical design comparison methodology, leveraging proprietary modeling tools to quantify loss reductions. The approach enables accurate performance assessment without requiring proprietary OEM data, offering a robust alternative for improving generator reliability and extending mean time between failures (MTBF). A new stator core and winding design is presented that demonstrates significant reductions in losses and temperature increases, leading to improved efficiency and extended generator lifespan. The research integrates insights from previous studies on motor losses and reliability improvements, further validating the proposed modifications.

articleTitle: Probabilistic Analysis of Power System Performance Under High PV and EV Penetration
abstract: This paper investigates the impact of high penetration levels of photovoltaic (PV) generation and electric vehicle charging stations (EVCS) on the operational efficiency of modern distribution grids. A probabilistic modeling framework is developed to address the uncertainties associated with PV generation, driven by weather variability, and EV charging demands, influenced by stochastic user behaviors. Using a modified version of the IEEE 123-bus system, various scenarios with different levels of PV and EVCS penetration are analyzed to evaluate their effects on voltage, power losses, and system reliability. Monte Carlo simulation is used to generate samples, while each sample realization is solved using an unbalanced voltage, var, and watt optimization (VVWO) model. Results demonstrate that coordination between PV and EVCS operations can mitigate the challenges posed by fluctuating renewable generation and increased EV demand. High PV penetration is shown to reduce power losses, support voltage stability, and minimize EVCS demand curtailment. The findings emphasize the importance of coordinated PV and EVCS management and offer insights for grid planners to enhance the hosting capacity of distribution networks.

articleTitle: An Efficient Resource Allocation Technique for Efficient Virtual Machine Placement Using Local Neighbor Search and Stochastic Random Process
abstract: Cloud computing environments efficiently utilize resources by managing diverse cloud users through virtualization techniques. Virtualization enhances resource utilization in Physical Machines (PMs). This paper introduces an efficient virtual machine placement algorithm based on an Improved Genetic Algorithm, which minimizes the Average Resource Idle Time of active PMs, thereby improving overall resource utilization in cloud data centers. Genetic Algorithms are effective optimization methods for achieving high accuracy with fewer iterations. However, they often encounter local optimum problems and quick convergence. The proposed algorithm addresses these issues and is implemented using the CloudSim Plus simulator in a standard cloud environment. Results indicate the algorithm reduces resource waiting time in PMs by approximately 52% compared to other algorithms. Additionally, it minimizes the Average Waiting Time and Average Turnaround Time for Virtual Machine placement. Performance analysis confirms its effectiveness, regardless of the number of Virtual Machine requests or available Physical Machines.

articleTitle: PV-Assisted Off-Board Electric Vehicle Charger for Low-Inertia Power System Stability: Virtual DC and AC Inertia Concepts
abstract: Accurate coordination between the DC-link and AC-side power of power electronic converters (PECs) employed in the electric vehicle off-board chargers (EVOBCs) can maximize the charging station (CS) contribution to the voltage stability of low-inertia power system (LIPS). This paper presents a novel approach for emulating the DC/DC and DC/AC converters of EVOBCs based on the virtual DC and AC inertia (VDCI-VACI) concepts. The proposed hybrid virtual inertia-based control system enables LIPS-side converter of EVOBC to generate the required VACI for the LIPS voltage stability through the on-time and precise injection of VDCIs made from the PV-connected and high voltage EV battery (HVEVB)-connected DC/DC converters. For further assessment, the VDCI and VACI generated in the PECs structures of EVOBCs are estimated using the global stability concept. The simulation results in MATLAB®/SIMULINK® environment are provided to confirm the validity of proposed method in different operation conditions.

articleTitle: RiskRadar: an Online Mapping Platform for Disaster Preparedness and Response via Comprehensive Data Integration and Visualization
abstract: Updatable and accurate mapping tools are essential for effective disaster management to safeguard public safety before, during, or after disasters. Maps help prioritize where assets are deployed in disasters in efficient ways and are important for compiling data layers about normal environmental risk inequalities of various indicators in general, to locate geographically the most vulnerable populations in order to improve their lives. Central to both kinds of mapping efforts are accessibility and clarity of information, whether in plotting a rapidly evolving natural or human-made hazard in a disaster zone, or for sharing with first responders, or for ongoing daily awareness and thus better administration about regular environmental risk in national populations. The RiskRadar platform prototype improves five shortcomings found regularly in other platforms for disaster risk reduction (DRR) and has more comprehensive data integration and visualization tools with its unique data indexes to enhance disaster preparedness and response. By integrating diverse environmental and urban data sets, RiskRadar shows different kinds of risk easily. From this, it facilitates informed decision-making on priorities and timely actions, while aiding more coordinated awareness and thus coordinated response to risk. This paper examines functionalities of a prototype platform for how it bolsters disaster resilience particularly in contexts desired by the United Nations Office for Disaster Risk Reduction (UNDRR). With a user-friendly interface, RiskRadar lets stakeholders, first responders, and the public at large access the same critical information. Good digitally-accessible maps aid better trust upon which better coordination for disaster management and higher group preparedness for future events can take place.

articleTitle: Exploring the Impact of Various Organic and Inorganic Electron Transport Layers in Highly Stable FA0.75MA0.25Sn0.95Ge0.05I3- Based Perovskite Solar Cells
abstract: Perovskite solar cells (PSCs) have garnered significant attention owing to their elevated efficiency, with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{FA}_{0.75}\mathbf{MA}_{0.25}\mathbf{Sn}_{0.95}\mathbf{Ge}_{0.05}\mathbf{I}_{3}$</tex> identified as a notable absorber material because of their high stability and cost-effectiveness. This research investigates the efficacy of the hybrid material as an absorber layer in conjunction with NiO as the hole transport layer (HTL) and several organic-inorganic electron transport layers (ETLs), namely <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{WS}_{2}$</tex>, PC <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${}_{60}\mathbf{BM}$</tex>, PFN <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$:\mathbf{Br}$</tex>, and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{ZnTe}$</tex>. The research employs SCAPS-1D numerical simulations to optimize key parameters, including the band diagram, thickness, and doping concentration of the absorber layer and ETL, to improve photovoltaic performance. The analysis demonstrates significant variations in power conversion efficiency (PCE) among configurations, contingent upon the selection of ETL. The <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{Glass}/\mathbf{FTO}/\mathbf{WS}_{2}/\mathbf{FA}_{0.75}\mathbf{MA}_{0.25}\mathbf{Sn}_{0.95}\mathbf{Ge}_{0.05}\mathbf{I}_{3}/\mathbf{NiO}/\mathbf{Au}$</tex> structure demonstrated optimal performance, with an open-circuit voltage <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\mathrm{V}_{\text{OC}})$</tex> of 1.12 V, a PCE of 31.01%, a fill factor (FF) of 88.21%, and a short-circuit current density <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\mathbf{J}_{\text{SC}})$</tex> of 31.12 m.A/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. Devices utilizing ETLs like PC <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${}_{60}\mathbf{BM}$</tex>, PFN:Br, and ZnT <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$e$</tex> achieved PCEs of 29.37%, 26.89%, and 29.70%, respectively. Furthermore, for all PSC structures, the associated current density-voltage (J-V) characteristics, generation rates, recombination rates, electron concentrations, and hole concentrations have been calculated. The findings indicate the importance of selecting a suitable ETL to optimize PSC performance.

articleTitle: NS3-Based Communication Network Modeling for Multi-Microgrid Systems: Design and Evaluation
abstract: This paper presents a communication emulation model for enhancing the efficiency of multi-microgrid (MMG) networks, employing Network Simulator 3 (ns3). MMG systems require robust communication frameworks for coordination, particularly under varying traffic conditions. The introduced model accommodates multiple local area networks (LANs) that support efficient communication across multiple autonomous AC microgrids. The developed model facilitates seamless bidirectional information exchange between the microgrids' local controllers and the MMG control center (MMGCC), employing TCP/IP protocol to ensure high data transmission integrity and low latency. A detailed design in C++ is demonstrated, including the configuration of the communication nodes, topology, communication links, and quality of service (QoS) analysis. The network performance is rigorously assessed across low and high traffic conditions, with performance metrics such as throughput, delay, and percentage packet loss at each node. Results confirm the effectiveness of the introduced model in sustaining minimal packet loss, high throughput, and low delays under dynamic operating scenarios. These findings establish the developed model as a viable solution for meeting the real-time communication requirements of MMG energy management systems.

articleTitle: Adoption of the IEEE 2800-2022 Standard by the Southwest Power Pool
abstract: This paper provides an overview of the Southwest Power Pool's (SPP) activities to adopt the IEEE 2800–2022 standard. It begins by evaluating various approaches to adoption and identifies the most practical and feasible approach for SPP, considering the technology readiness levels of vendors and the concerns of generator owners, transmission owners, transmission operators, and consultants. The paper then summarizes the results of a gap analysis conducted by SPP, comparing SPP governance documents with IEEE 2800–2022 clauses. Following this, the paper introduces and proposes a phased plan for adoption, developed through negotiations and discussions between SPP staff and stakeholders, spanning from late 2022 to the end of 2024. Next, it outlines the modifications made to SPP governance documents to support the first phase of adoption. Finally, the paper discusses the gaps, challenges and concerns, final revisions and recommendations, and future work necessary for the full adoption of the standard by SPP.

articleTitle: An Optimal Dispatch Model for Economic Benefit Valuation of Grid Energy Storage Solutions
abstract: Diverse grid energy storage applications establish varied cost and performance targets for emerging battery technologies. Optimal dispatch models that target specific energy storage applications and incorporate key battery performance characteristics are crucial for evaluating the economic benefits of these promising technologies. For applications such as energy time shifting (ETS), energy arbitrage, and renewable integration, existing economic dispatch models either overlook essential battery dynamics or fail to simplify complex nonlinear constraints, resulting in less realistic and more computationally challenging optimizations. To address this issue, this study proposes an optimal energy dispatch model that aims to maximize operational revenue of a battery energy storage system (BESS) while modeling battery behavior by introducing the simplest equivalent circuit model into the constraints. The model's nonlinear constraints are relaxed into linear representations to formulate a mixed-integer linear programming problem. A case study on ETS in the real-time market demonstrates that the vanadium redox flow and sodium-ion BESSs achieve higher daily revenue than the lithium-ion BESS. Additionally, higher C-rates (the rate at which a battery charges or discharges relative to its capacity) and stronger power capabilities enable these BESSs to cycle more frequently and better capitalize on price differences, thereby generating greater profit. These findings indicate that the proposed model effectively evaluates the economic performance of various battery technologies in an ETS application.

articleTitle: Sustainable Bamboo Greenhouse with Integrated Rainwater Harvesting System
abstract: This work presents a novel bamboo greenhouse with integrated rainwater harvesting (RWH) to sustainably address water scarcity and food insecurity in vulnerable communities. The “Juciri”-like structure features a unique hexagonal geometry and sloped roof to maximize rainwater capture and optimize cultivation space. Structural analyses compared bamboo (Guadua angustifolia) and galvanized steel as construction materials. Results show bamboo, with a dead load of 72.27 kg, provides adequate structural performance under loads, with a maximum displacement of 0.77 cm-closely matching steel but with significantly lower weight and cost. Showing a relative flexibility index for bending moments of 11.90% and a 45.42% less cost in front of galvanized steel. Environmental assessments using Life Cycle Assessment focused on Global Warming Potential (GWP100), Acidification Potential (AP), and Ozone Depletion Potential (ODP). The bamboo structure's GWP was 3.80 kg CO2-eq, over 95% lower than steel's 87.97 kg CO2-eq. The RWH system collects up to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$23.3 \mathrm{L}/\mathrm{m}^{2}$</tex> per month from its <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$17.67 \mathrm{m}^{2}$</tex> area, ensuring reliable irrigation. Clay pot irrigation improves water efficiency by delivering moisture directly to roots, reducing evaporation and eliminating PVC use. Locally sourced bamboo minimizes environmental impacts and fosters community self-reliance through job creation. Its lightweight, cost-effective design enables self-construction and scalability to various regions. This approach offers a sustainable solution to enhance food and water security, strengthening vulnerable communities against climate change.

articleTitle: Improved Subsynchronous Frequency Oscillations Detection in Wind Farms Using AI-based Fourier Transformation and Advanced Metrics
abstract: Low-Frequency oscillations in wind farms, caused by interactions between power converters and transmission lines, must be addressed quickly to prevent grid instability. While past studies using Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) have focused on high-magnitude oscillation detection, these methods often demand substantial data and computational resources, delaying detection and causing substantial damage to the grid. Moreover, the issue of low-frequency oscillations, which can lead to high-frequency resonance and potential power outages, remains underexplored. In this paper, we propose a dual detection system that swiftly identifies high-magnitude oscillations through time-domain analysis and detects low-frequency oscillations using Fast Fourier Transform-based frequency-domain analysis. We employ Hyperdimensional Computing (HDC) along with one-class SVM introducing True Positive Confidence (TPC) and False Positive Confidence (FPC) metrics to enhance reliability. Our findings show HDC surpasses One class SVM model, performing 6x faster on GPU and 16x on FPGA achieving at least 99% confidence in TPC and FPC for the oscillation types of interest in this work. This positions HDC as an optimal solution for real-time wind farm applications, offering significant advantages in speed and accuracy. Most importantly, the proposed solutions can detect oscillations within tens of microseconds, significantly ahead of the critical time window of 500/800 μ<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$s$</tex> from the onset of the oscillation, ensuring timely and reliable fault detection.
